symptom: console.log(JSON.stringify(...)) followed by process.exit() silently truncates on a pipe at the buffer size (~8 KB on macOS). Present in verify-harness --json and six other shipped scripts since they were written. Surfaced only when aeron-demo's report crossed 8 KB and adoption-baseline could no longer parse its own input — before that, every --json consumer had been fine by luck of payload size.
remedy: writeSync(1, ...) everywhere a JSON payload precedes process.exit. Demo now statically scans every shipped .mjs for the pattern and round-trips a real report through spawnSync.

note: all seven scripts converted to writeSync; verified aeron-demo's 8238-byte report now parses through spawnSync, and demo.sh scans for the pattern so it cannot return.

symptom: setup-harness-loop.mjs skips every existing file, which is right for project-owned content (AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, docs/architecture.md) and wrong for skill-owned machinery. Same class already hit tools/*.mjs twice: an upgraded skill does not reach an existing target.
remedy: an --upgrade mode that refreshes the skill-owned set (tools/**, loop/run-loop.sh, loop/route.mjs, loop/approval-gate.mjs, check-coverage.mjs, docs/reference/**, skills/**) and never touches the project-owned set. symptom: feature-planner re-cut aeron-demo to 54 features and reported '0 blockers throughout' — while shipping 0/54 falsifiers and 0/54 kind tags. Its self-check step named only scope-smell, and every check that exists to catch the PLANNER is a warning by design (so adoption is not a wall). So the agent passed its own gate with the oracle layer left nothing to derive from.

symptom: adoption-baseline reported build-unproven 0 -> 13 as NEW DEBT. Nothing got worse: the check is opt-in on the kind tag, no feature had one at adoption, so it was dormant and only started measuring when the planner added kind. Turning on a previously-silent gate is indistinguishable from a regression.
remedy: record which gates were dormant at --record time (a gate with a known opt-in precondition that was unmet), and report their first non-zero count as 'newly measured' rather than 'new debt'. Until then the operator has to know which gates are opt-in.

symptom: feat-ledger-core was APPROVED done on attempt 3 of 3 — the loop working exactly as intended — and verify-harness immediately raised a blocker: 'attempts=3 >= maxAttempts=3 but status is done, not blocked'. The timebox check only excludes status=blocked, so succeeding on the last allowed attempt is indistinguishable from exhausting the budget without finishing.
remedy: exclude terminal success (done/passing) as well as blocked. The check exists to stop silent infinite retrying, and a feature that finished is not retrying.

note: timebox check now excludes done/passing as well as blocked; verified on aeron-demo (1 blocker -> 0) and asserted in demo.sh both directions.

symptom: The checker logged two real follow-ups on a feature it APPROVED — a deprecated overload that silently drops state and would reintroduce the fixed defect, plus stale comments. They live in the checkerNotes of a done feature, which nothing routes on: NEEDS DESIGN and NEEDS RE-PLAN are for rejections, and the maker only picks eligible not-started features. A non-blocking finding is therefore recorded and then invisible.
remedy: either a FOLLOW-UP: marker the router reads and hands to the planner, or an explicit instruction that the checker must choose between blocking and letting it go. Recording something nobody will act on is the worst of the three options. Sixth instance of detector-without-a-route this session.

symptom: scope-smell fires on EITHER >400 chars OR >=3 and/then joiners. On the BOD re-plan it produced 5 findings; the operator judged all 5 individually and found each to be a single claim - long because a prove feature narrates a sequential scenario (apply BOD, then snapshot, then restart, then read) or enumerates the cases one contract covers. Length is a weak proxy for compound structure on scenario features specifically.
remedy: DO NOT tune the threshold to reduce a count on one project - that is weakening a gate because you dislike its output, and AGENTS.md makes it a human checkpoint. Recorded as one data point. If a second project shows the same pattern, weight clause structure over raw length and give kind:prove more narrative room than kind:build.
